$comment: The merge conveyor. A tick can merge, so only its timer runs one: `tick` (`--dry-run` alone passes) and the timer script are refused, read per program so a commit message or a grep that mentions them passes; the parser reads `pnpm run x` and `sh file` as no program, so those two rows read the command as typed. A subcommand the guard can't read may be `tick`: it asks. A raw post of the `conveyor/cleared` status opens a merge: refused, by curl (both words on one line; reading or grepping it is fine) or `gh api` (statusContexts). Starting it (CONVEYOR_ENABLED to anything but `off`) or deleting the variable asks, by gh, `gh api`, or curl.

deny.reason: A tick can merge, so only the conveyor's timer runs it. `pnpm conveyor tick --dry-run` and `pnpm conveyor status` show what it would see.

ask.reason: The guard can't read which conveyor subcommand this runs, and `tick` can merge. Name it: `pnpm conveyor clear|status|report`.
CONVEYOR_ENABLED decides whether the timer merges, so starting it or removing the variable is the user's call. `--body off` stops it and needs no asking.
